es: Reconocer generalizaciones matizadas (tend to, be supposed to, it is customary to) y distinguir costumbre general, norma esperada y excepción.

teaching.en: In many countries it is customary to bring a small gift when you visit a family.
teaching.es: En muchos países es costumbre llevar un pequeño regalo cuando visitas a una familia.
teaching.explanationEs: It is customary to + verbo describe una costumbre aceptada por una comunidad.
segments: In many countries it is customary to bring
a small gift when you visit a family.
teaching.audioText: In many countries it is customary to bring a small gift when you visit a family.

teaching.en: Hosts tend to offer something to drink as soon as guests arrive.
teaching.es: Los anfitriones suelen ofrecer algo de beber en cuanto llegan los invitados.
teaching.explanationEs: Tend to + verbo base expresa lo que suele ocurrir, sin decir que ocurra siempre.
segments: Hosts tend to offer something to
drink as soon as guests arrive.
teaching.audioText: Hosts tend to offer something to drink as soon as guests arrive.

teaching.en: You are supposed to be punctual for a job interview, but a dinner with friends is more relaxed.
teaching.es: Se supone que debes ser puntual en una entrevista de trabajo, pero una cena con amigos es más relajada.
teaching.explanationEs: Be supposed to expresa lo que se espera de ti según la norma.
segments: You are supposed to be punctual for a job
interview, but a dinner with friends is more relaxed.
teaching.audioText: You are supposed to be punctual for a job interview, but a dinner with friends is more relaxed.

teaching.en: Generally, colleagues shake hands when they meet for the first time.
teaching.es: Por lo general, los compañeros se dan la mano la primera vez que se conocen.
teaching.explanationEs: Generally abre una generalización que deja espacio a otras posibilidades.

teaching.en: Every custom has an exception, so avoid saying that everybody does it.
teaching.es: Toda costumbre tiene una excepción, así que evita decir que todo el mundo lo hace.
teaching.explanationEs: La excepción recuerda que una generalización nunca describe a todos.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase describe lo que suele ocurrir, sin ser una obligación?

choices.text: In many homes, guests tend to bring dessert.
Guests must wait for the host before eating.
Not every guest brings dessert, though.

feedback.es: Tend to describe una costumbre frecuente; la frase con must marca una obligación y la de not every guest, una excepción.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que significa «suele» y no «debe».

prompt.es: Completa: «Se supone que debes quitarte los zapatos al entrar.»

feedback.es: Be supposed to expresa lo que se espera de ti según la norma.

hint.es: Es la palabra de la clase que marca lo que se espera de ti.

origin.text: You are ___ to take off your shoes when you come in.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los anfitriones suelen ofrecer té a los invitados.»

answer.text: Hosts tend to offer tea to guests

feedback.es: Tend va seguido de to y del verbo base: tend to offer.

hint.es: Tend va seguido de to y del verbo base.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada descripción con su tipo.

pairs: Most neighbours say hello on the stairs.
Students are supposed to switch off their phones in class.
Not everybody shakes hands; some people only smile.

feedback.es: Decir hola en las escaleras es lo habitual, apagar el móvil es lo que se espera y not everybody señala una excepción.

prompt.es: Completa con la expresión que significa: suelen · es costumbre · por lo general

feedback.es: Families tend to describe lo que suele pasar, it is customary nombra una costumbre y generally abre una generalización.

sentences: Families ___ to eat together on Sundays.
It is ___ to bring a small gift.
___, people shake hands when they meet.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige quién es la excepción.

choices.text: The man who always waves first.
The man who never waves back.
The children who wave from the window.

feedback.es: Lo habitual es saludar con la mano en la calle; el hombre que nunca devuelve el saludo es la excepción.

origin.audio: In my village, people usually wave at each other in the street. Most of them wave back, but one man never does.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase expresa una norma esperada y no una costumbre general?

choices.text: Visitors tend to bring a small gift.
It is customary to say thank you.
Visitors are supposed to remove their shoes at the door.

feedback.es: Are supposed to marca lo que se espera de los visitantes; las otras dos describen lo que suele hacerse.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del texto es la excepción?

choices.text: Ana's boss only smiles and waves.
Colleagues tend to shake hands.
They are supposed to be punctual.

feedback.es: La jefa de Ana no sigue lo que suelen hacer los demás: solo sonríe y saluda con la mano.

origin.text: In many offices, colleagues tend to shake hands on the first day. They are supposed to be punctual. Ana's boss, however, only smiles and waves.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se espera del invitado al principio.

choices.text: To eat everything at once.
To say no politely to the first offer.
To bring his own food.

feedback.es: El invitado debe rechazar con cortesía la primera oferta; después acepta. Y no todas las familias lo hacen.

origin.audio: In some families, a guest is supposed to refuse the first offer of food politely. The host offers again, and then the guest accepts. Not every family follows this custom, though.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Es costumbre llevar un postre cuando visitas a unos amigos.»

answer.text: It is customary to bring a dessert when you visit friends
accepted: It is customary to bring a dessert when you visit friends
When you visit friends it is customary to bring a dessert
When you visit friends, it is customary to bring a dessert

feedback.es: It is customary to + verbo base nombra una costumbre aceptada.

choices.text: All people here eat lunch at noon, without exception.
People here never eat lunch at noon, not even on Sundays.
In general, people here eat lunch at noon, but some eat later.

feedback.es: In general y but some eat later dejan espacio a excepciones; all y never afirman lo absoluto.
Every + sustantivo singular pide has: una generalización siempre admite excepciones.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué espera la familia de Sara de sus invitados.

choices.text: That they stay for coffee after dinner.
That they leave right after dinner.
That they bring the coffee.

feedback.es: La norma en casa de Sara es quedarse a tomar café; su primo es la excepción.

origin.audio: Sara says that in her family, guests are supposed to stay for coffee after dinner. Her cousin is the exception, because he always leaves early.
